AURORA-WELL-01
A Randomized, Controlled Pilot Study of a Digital Wellness Program for Improving Daily Activity
and Sleep Routine Consistency in Adult Volunteers

AURORA-WELL-01 | Synthetic Clinical Protocol
Version 1.1 | 04 October 2026
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Page 2
1. Protocol Synopsis
Item
Description
Primary objective
Evaluate whether a structured digital wellness program improves consistency of daily activity
over 12 weeks.
Secondary objectives
Evaluate sleep timing regularity, engagement, usability, retention, and data completeness.
Design
Two-week baseline, eight-week intervention, and two-week follow-up; randomized 1:1.
Intervention
Digital reminders, weekly planning prompts, activity goal setting, and sleep-routine education.
Control
Static wellness information without adaptive reminders or weekly planning prompts.
Primary endpoint
Change from baseline in the percentage of evaluable days meeting a participant-specific
activity window.
Duration
Up to 14 weeks per participant, including screening and closeout.
1.1 Schedule Overview
Period
Weeks
Main activities
Screening
-2 to 0
Consent, eligibility, demographics, and device compatibility
Baseline
0 to 2
Passive activity capture, sleep diary, and questionnaires
Intervention
2 to 10
Assigned study content, weekly planning, and data capture
Follow-up
10 to 12
Final passive capture, questionnaires, and closeout
The intervention does not provide diagnosis, treatment, emergency monitoring, or medical advice.

AURORA-WELL-01 | Synthetic Clinical Protocol
Version 1.1 | 04 October 2026
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Page 3
2. Background and Rationale
Regular daily activity and consistent sleep timing are common behavioral indicators in wellness research. Routine
variability may arise from work schedules, travel, caregiving, and competing demands. Digital planning tools may help
participants organize daily routines, although engagement can decline when reminders are excessive or poorly timed.
AURORA-WELL-01 is a low-risk software-enabled pilot study. The program provides general planning prompts rather
than a medical intervention. The study is intended to estimate feasibility, retention, engagement, and endpoint variability
before a larger investigation.
Figure 2. Conceptual study journey from screening through follow-up and analysis. Synthetic visual included to test image
extraction and S3 asset persistence.
2.1 Rationale for the Program
•
Weekly planning supports realistic activity and sleep windows.
•
Daily reminders are limited and may be snoozed.
•
Progress summaries emphasize consistency rather than competition.
•
Participants may stop optional prompts at any time.

AURORA-WELL-01 | Synthetic Clinical Protocol
Version 1.1 | 04 October 2026
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Page 4
3. Objectives and Endpoints
Level
Objective
Endpoint
Primary
Assess change in activity regularity
Change in percentage of evaluable days inside the selected
activity window
Secondary
Assess sleep timing regularity
Change in standard deviation of nightly sleep midpoint
Secondary
Assess engagement
Proportion of intervention weeks with a completed planning
interaction
Secondary
Assess retention
Proportion completing the Week 12 assessment
Secondary
Assess usability
Mean score on the study usability questionnaire
Exploratory
Explore daytime functioning
Change in a short self-reported functioning scale
3.1 Endpoint Rules
•
A day is evaluable when at least 10 hours of device availability is recorded.
•
Sleep midpoint is derived from participant-entered sleep and wake times after plausibility checks.
•
Timestamps are converted to participant-local time.
•
Temporary interruptions use available data under the prespecified analysis strategy.
3.2 Sample Size Rationale
A total of 120 randomized participants, approximately 60 per group, is expected to provide adequate precision for
feasibility estimates. Assuming up to 15% attrition, approximately 102 participants are expected to contribute to the
primary analysis.

Version 1.1 | 04 October 2026

Page 5
4. Study Design and Population
After a two-week baseline period, eligible participants are assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the digital wellness program or
control condition. Assignment is stratified by baseline activity regularity and study site.
4.1 Study Flow
Stage
Activity
Output
Screening
Confirm eligibility, consent, and smartphone compatibility
Screened participant
Baseline
Collect at least 7 activity days and 5 sleep diaries
Baseline-qualified participant
Randomization
Apply centralized allocation with concealed variable block sizes
Assigned group
Intervention
Deliver assigned content and collect engagement data
Intervention dataset
Follow-up
Collect final passive data and questionnaires
Completed participant record
4.2 Inclusion Criteria
•
Age 21 to 65 years.
•
Able to provide informed consent.
•
Owns a compatible smartphone.
•
Reports an irregular activity or sleep routine.
•
Willing to complete brief electronic questionnaires.
4.3 Exclusion Criteria
•
Conflicting research participation.
•
Planned prolonged travel across more than three time zones.
•
Recent use of a similar structured wellness program.
•
Investigator determination that participation is unsuitable.

6. Data Management, Privacy, and Security
Study data are captured through electronic forms, the study application, and device synchronization services.
Automated checks identify missing fields, implausible dates, duplicate submissions, and out-of-window assessments.
Corrections require an audit trail.
Figure 3. Conceptual secure data flow across participant devices, cloud services, and research systems. Synthetic visual
included to test embedded-image extraction.
6.1 Privacy Controls
•
Direct identifiers are stored separately from coded study records.
•
Access is restricted by study role and reviewed periodically.
•
Data exports use encrypted transfer and controlled storage locations.
•
Retention and deletion follow the approved data-management plan.
6.2 Analysis Populations
Population
Definition
Enrolled
All individuals who provide informed consent
Randomized
All participants assigned to a group
Primary analysis
Randomized participants meeting minimum evaluable-data requirements
Per-protocol
Participants without major eligibility or data deviations
Safety summary
Participants who begin the assigned study condition

Version 1.1 | 04 October 2026
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Page 8
7. Safety and Quality Oversight
Participants are instructed to report unfavorable experiences associated with study participation. Personnel document
reported events, assess seriousness and relatedness, and follow site reporting procedures. The application does not
provide emergency monitoring.
7.1 Event Categories
Category
Example
Action
Application issue
Unexpected notification or synchronization
failure
Document, troubleshoot, and assess effect on study
data
Participation burden
Excessive reminders or questionnaire fatigue
Adjust optional reminders and document preference
Physical experience
Temporary discomfort during voluntary activity
Stop activity and seek appropriate care if required
Privacy concern
Suspected unauthorized access
Escalate under the privacy incident procedure
7.2 Quality Control
•
Complete site training before participant-facing activity.
•
Use required-field and range checks in key forms.
•
Review a sample of consent, eligibility, and endpoint records.
•
Resolve or document data queries before database lock.
•
Version analysis datasets and derivation specifications.
7.3 Protocol Deviations
A protocol deviation is any departure from the approved procedures or participant instructions. Deviations are
documented, assessed for impact on participant rights and data reliability, and reviewed for corrective action.
End of Protocol

Choose a period of the day when ordinary activity is usually possible. The study does not require

participant.
Morning: 06:00 to 10:00
Midday: 10:00 to 14:00

Stop any voluntary activity that causes discomfort. The study application is not an emergency service
and does not provide medical advice. Contact an appropriate healthcare professional for health concerns
and local emergency services for urgent situations.
